title: Dephasing-induced distinct mobility edges in a dimerized off-diagonal quasicrystal
authors: Ming-Jie Tao, Yi-Ting Wang, Jing Li, Hongsheng Hou, Xiang-Ping Jiang, Lei Pan
abstract: Anderson localization and the mobility edge (ME) have been extensively studied in isolated aperiodic systems. Conventional theory suggests that dephasing and decoherence should disrupt localization and facilitate transport. In this work, we investigate localization behaviors in a dimerized off-diagonal Aubry-Andre-Harper (AAH) quasicrystal subject to on-site pure dephasing. In the strong-dephasing limit, we apply adiabatic elimination within the Lindblad master equation framework to derive an effective classical Markov transition matrix that governs the dissipative relaxation dynamics. Counterintuitively, we demonstrate that pure dephasing can induce distinct MEs, including both conventional MEs separating extended and localized states and anomalous MEs separating multifractal critical states from localized states, even when all eigenstates of the original closed coherent system are delocalized or multifractal. Using fractal dimension finite-size scaling, wave-packet spreading dynamics, and energy spectrum statistics, we numerically verify the coexistence of fully extended, multifractal critical, and localized regions within the relaxation spectrum of the dissipative system, and construct the global dissipative phase diagram. These findings reveal that dephasing can see as a powerful mechanism for controlling localization transitions, thus enhancing our understanding of dissipative quasicrystal systems.
summary: This work analyzes localization in a quasiperiodic quantum system subjected to pure dephasing. By mapping the dynamics to an effective classical Markov process, the authors demonstrate that dephasing induces distinct mobility edges. This reveals that dephasing is a powerful mechanism capable of stabilizing and controlling multiple distinct transport regimes (extended, critical, localized) within the system's spectrum.
main_problem: The paper investigates how pure dephasing affects localization behavior in a dimerized off-diagonal Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) quasicrystal.
main_result: Pure dephasing can induce distinct Mobility Edges (MEs), including anomalous ones, allowing for the coexistence of extended, multifractal critical, and localized states in the dissipative system.
method: The analysis uses the Lindblad master equation, applying adiabatic elimination in the strong-dephasing limit to derive an effective classical Markov transition matrix.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D tight-binding model of free spinless fermions on a dimerized off-diagonal AAH quasicrystal, governed by a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), fractal dimension ($\Gamma_k$), wave-packet spreading variance ($\sigma^2(t)$), and level spacing statistics.
important_parameters: Dephasing rate ($\gamma$), quasiperiodic modulation strength ($\lambda, V$), and the ratio of dephasing to hopping ($ \gamma \gg t$).
main_assumptions: The strong-dephasing limit ($\gamma \gg t$) allows for the adiabatic elimination of coherence terms, reducing the dynamics to a classical Markov process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the global phase diagram in $(\lambda, V)$ space showing boundaries for extended, critical, and localized phases, alongside time evolution plots of wave-packet variance ($\sigma^2(t)$) confirming different transport regimes.
paper_structure: The paper reviews localization in closed systems, introduces the open system formalism via the Lindblad equation, and finally applies the strong-dephasing limit to derive the Markov matrix and construct the global dissipative phase diagram.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete example of how environmental coupling (dephasing) can actively control and reshape localization transitions in complex quasiperiodic systems, moving beyond the simple expectation of decoherence always destroying localization.

FIG. 5. Global phase diagram of the dissipative sys- tem in the (λ, V ) parameter space in the strong-dephasing regime. Boundaries mark three distinct spectral regimes: the fully-extended regime, a mixed regime of extended and lo- calized states, and a mixed regime of critical and localized states, separated by conventional MEs and AMEs.
